accepted.s: The South Coast Railway zone was created under which statutory provision?
accepted.x: The South Coast Railway zone was mandated by the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
accepted.tq: Match the railway zone with the correct parent legislation.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the restructuring of railway divisions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Visakhapatnam division was formed from the truncated Waltair division of East Coast Railway.
2. The Vijayawada, Guntur and Guntakal divisions came from South Central Railway.
3. The remaining part of Waltair division forms the new Rayagada division of East Coast Railway.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Visakhapatnam came from the truncated Waltair division, the other three divisions came from South Central Railway, and the remaining Waltair area became ECoR’s Rayagada division.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the source railway zone of each division.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following railway establishments continues to remain under South Central Railway after the formation of South Coast Railway?
accepted.x: South Central Railway retains Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Nanded. Visakhapatnam, Guntur and Guntakal are associated with South Coast Railway.
accepted.tq: Use the retained-membership trap in a reorganisation question.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Railway project)
a. Errupalem–Nambur line
b. Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line
c. Kotipalli–Narasapur line

d. Rajahmundry–Visakhapatnam third/fourth lines

List-II (Relevant feature)
i. Work in progress along the Konaseema coast
 ii. 57 km line with a 3-km bridge over the Krishna
 iii. 308 km line serving four backward districts
 iv. Project costing ₹9,889 crore

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Errupalem–Nambur is the 57-km Amaravati line with a Krishna bridge; Nadikudi–Srikalahasti is 308 km; Kotipalli–Narasapur is under way on the Konaseema coast; and the Rajahmundry–Visakhapatnam third/fourth lines cost ₹9,889 crore.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing mismatched project features.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Errupalem–Nambur Amaravati railway line?
o: It includes a 30-km bridge over the Krishna.
It passes through NTR and Guntur districts.
accepted.x: The Amaravati line includes a 3-km bridge over the Krishna, not a 30-km bridge. It is a 57-km broad-gauge line through NTR and Guntur districts.
accepted.tq: Find the numerical exaggeration in an otherwise familiar project description.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti railway line is particularly associated with the movement of:
o: Coal and petroleum from coastal ports
accepted.x: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line is intended to support cement and granite traffic and serves Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore and Chittoor.
accepted.tq: Link the infrastructure project with its stated freight purpose.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about railway development in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The railway network of Andhra Pradesh is fully electrified.
2. Works valued at ₹92,649 crore are under way.
3. Twenty-one of South Central Railway’s 73 Amrit Bharat stations are in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: AP’s network is 100% electrified, works worth ₹92,649 crore are under way, and 21 of SCR’s 73 Amrit Bharat stations are in the State.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the last eleven years, which one of the following combinations correctly represents railway infrastructure created or completed in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 3,748 km new lines, 1,217 km doubling and 414 km electrification
414 km new lines, 1,217 km doubling and 3,748 km electrification
1,217 km new lines, 414 km doubling and 3,748 km electrification
414 km doubling, 1,217 km electrification and 3,748 km new lines
accepted.x: The reported figures are 414 km of new lines, 1,217 km of doubling and 3,748 km of electrification.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of three closely related quantitative categories.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Vijayawada railway station’s Platinum certification is awarded by:
accepted.x: Vijayawada station holds IGBC Platinum certification from the Indian Green Building Council. The attribution to LEED, USA is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar green-building certification bodies.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The FY 2026 railway budget allocation for Andhra Pradesh was reported as:
accepted.x: The FY 2026 railway budget allocation for Andhra Pradesh was ₹9,417 crore. ₹10,134 crore refers to another reported railway allocation figure, while the other values relate to works or highway expenditure.
accepted.tq: Separate budget allocation from project-value figures.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Amaravati railway line is correctly described as:
o: A 308-km line between Nadikudi and Srikalahasti costing ₹9,889 crore
A 125-km line linking Narketpally and Addanki under PPP
A coastal line between Kotipalli and Narasapur costing ₹2,245 crore
A 57-km broad-gauge line between Errupalem and Nambur costing ₹2,245 crore
accepted.x: The Amaravati line is the 57-km Errupalem–Nambur broad-gauge line, costing ₹2,245 crore and including a 3-km Krishna bridge.
accepted.tq: Use the project-name and route-name pairing to reject cross-matched alternatives.
accepted.sec: Railway network of AP - South Coast Railway zone HQ and divisions, new lines  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s National Highway density per lakh population is higher than the Indian average by approximately:
accepted.x: AP’s density is 17.64 km per lakh population and India’s is 12.09 km; the difference is 5.55 km per lakh population.
accepted.tq: Calculate the difference rather than merely recalling the larger figure.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding National Highway density in Andhra Pradesh:
1. AP has 17.64 km of National Highways per lakh population.
2. India has 12.09 km of National Highways per lakh population.
3. AP has 53.65 km of National Highways per 1,000 square kilometres, against India’s 44.46 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly state the population-based and area-based highway-density figures.
accepted.tq: Compare paired State and national indicators without reversing the comparison.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which authority controls the largest share of the National Highway length in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: NHAI controls 4,406 km, compared with 3,738 km under the State PWD and 600 km under the MoRTH-PIU.
accepted.tq: Compare institutional responsibility by the size of the controlled network.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match the following National Highway control agencies with the length under their control:

a. NHAI
b. MoRTH–PIU
c. State PWD

i. 600 km
 ii. 3,738 km
 iii. 4,406 km

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NHAI controls 4,406 km, MoRTH–PIU controls 600 km and the State PWD controls 3,738 km.
accepted.tq: Begin with the largest agency figure and verify the remaining pairs.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding National Highway works in Andhra Pradesh during FY 2025–26 is correct?
o: 392 works covering 93 km were completed, with an expenditure of ₹45,633 crore.
93 works covering 392 km were sanctioned, with an expenditure of ₹2,065 crore.
93 works covering 2,065 km were sanctioned, with an expenditure of ₹45,633 crore.
2,065 works covering 93 km were sanctioned, with an expenditure of ₹1.40 lakh crore.
accepted.x: During FY 2025–26, 93 works covering 2,065 km involved ₹45,633 crore; 392 km had been completed.
accepted.tq: Keep work count, route length, cost and completed length distinct.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor is designated as:
accepted.x: The Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor is designated NH-544G and is targeted for completion by 2027.
accepted.tq: Match the economic corridor with its specific National Highway number.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about economic corridors and expressways associated with Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor is targeted for completion by 2027.
2. The Nagpur–Vijayawada greenfield expressway has been fast-tracked.
3. The Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati expressway has been fast-tracked and a DPR has been ordered.
4. The Narketpally–Addanki–Medarametla road is a 125-km PPP project linking NH-65 and NH-16.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Narketpally–Addanki–Medarametla road is the completed 125-km PPP link between NH-65 and NH-16.
accepted.tq: Treat each corridor as a separate project-status and route-length clue.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: NH-544G is the Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor. The Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati project is a separate fast-tracked expressway for which a DPR was ordered.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped highway identity among otherwise familiar route pairs.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Highway works planned in Andhra Pradesh by 2029 are valued at:
accepted.x: National Highway projects worth over ₹1.40 lakh crore are planned to be completed by 2029. ₹42,194 crore is the target mentioned for 2027.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the long-term target from the intermediate-year target.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The target for National Highway projects in Andhra Pradesh by 2027 is approximately:
accepted.x: The target mentioned for 2027 is ₹42,194 crore, while the broader 2029 target exceeds ₹1.40 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Separate intermediate targets from the final programme value.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following National Highway-related targets or projects in chronological order of the stated completion or implementation stage:
A. Completion target for the Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor
B. Completion target for ₹42,194 crore worth of highway projects
C. Completion target for highway projects worth over ₹1.40 lakh crore
D. Completion of the Narketpally–Addanki–Medarametla PPP road

Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: The Narketpally–Addanki–Medarametla road is already completed; the corridor target is 2027, the ₹42,194-crore target is also for 2027, and the ₹1.40-lakh-crore target is for 2029. Since the two 2027 targets are parallel, the sequence places the completed project first, followed by the 2027 targets and then 2029.
accepted.tq: Fix the completed project first and place the dated targets after it.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proposed Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati expressway is presently associated with:
o: Fast-tracking and preparation of a Detailed Project Report
Completion as a PPP road linking NH-65 and NH-16
A completed four-lane railway line through NTR district
accepted.x: The Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati expressway has been fast-tracked and a DPR has been ordered.
accepted.tq: Match a project’s present status with the action actually reported for it.
accepted.sec: National highways in AP - number, longest NH, Bharatmala and economic corridors  [APPSC]
